breaks.detail: Half the claim matrix here is negative/blocking ("cancel WITHOUT a reason must be REJECTED, booking stays ACCEPTED"). Mechanism 1.1 (write-set-bound oracle) binds a WORKS claim to an OBSERVED delta. A blocked-cancel claim's correct outcome is NO delta -- which is trivially satisfied by an agent that never clicks submit at all. As written, the theory has no explicit effect-check shape for 'attempted mutation, observed rejection, null delta' -- it needs a positive receipt that the submit action was actually fired (network request captured out-of-band, e.g. the cancel endpoint call and its 4xx response) PLUS the null store-diff, not just the null diff alone. Without that add-on, a lazy/failed agent walk and a correctly-blocked walk are indistinguishable to the harness.
breaks.fix: Add a day-one effect-check variant: for any pre-registered negative/blocking claim, require an attempted-action receipt (captured request+response for the mutating call) in addition to the null persisted-state delta; NOT-EXECUTED (no attempt receipt) -> CND, same as the existing rule for missing positive effect checks.

breaks.detail: The quantifier lint (1.4) requires >=2 distinct in-scope instantiations that are NOT the configuring actor. Here the two actors are 'host' and 'attendee', but on cal.com these aren't just two form-field labels -- isCancellationUserHost is derived server-side from session-email-equals-organizer-email, and the attendee normally reaches the cancel UI via an anonymous booking-link URL (/booking/[uid]) with NO login, while the host reaches it via an authenticated dashboard route. If the harness's cross-exam driver models 'switch actor' as just changing a name/email typed into a form rather than genuinely tearing down the authenticated session/cookie jar, the 'attendee' walk can silently re-execute inside the host's still-authenticated browser context. The code then takes the host branch, and a test intended to prove 'attendee is blocked' actually re-proves 'host is blocked' -- a false WORKS via session leakage, structurally identical to owner-shadow (FW-11) but caused by auth-context conflation rather than data quantifier collapse.
breaks.fix: Extend 1.4's quantifier lint with an explicit auth-context check: the harness must independently verify (via a receipt -- absence of an auth cookie, or a session/user-id marker on the request) that the 'not the configuring actor' leg ran under a genuinely distinct (or anonymous) identity, not merely trust the agent's narration that it 'switched actors.'

breaks.detail: The diff shows the zod input schema (BaseEventTypeUpdateInput) and the managed-props allowlists gaining requiresCancellationReason, matching the pattern used by disableCancelling/disableRescheduling. But the actual tRPC mutation handler that consumes the validated input and calls prisma.eventType.update(...) is NOT in the diff -- its inclusion is inferred by pattern-matching against sibling flags, not confirmed. If that handler explicitly allowlists fields rather than spreading validated input, the setting could validate and save 200 OK client-side while never reaching the database -- a classic explains-but-doesn't-persist gap the P' oracle is specifically designed to catch (write-set-bound diff on EventType would show no row change), but only if the walk actually saves the setting through the UI rather than seeding it via fixture/migration default.
breaks.fix: Before scoring, the harness must exercise the ENTIRE chain front-door: open Event Type Advanced tab, pick a non-default option (e.g. MANDATORY_BOTH), save, and diff the EventType row for requiresCancellationReason -- not just seed the DB column directly and jump straight to the cancel-flow test (that would be fixture-world divergence, FW-12).

compiledPromise: Discriminating claim (positive): 'When an EventType's requiresCancellationReason is set to MANDATORY_ATTENDEE_ONLY, an attendee who attempts to cancel their own booking through the public booking-detail page (/booking/[uid], no login) WITHOUT typing a cancellation reason is blocked -- the cancel submit is rejected, the Booking.status row stays ACCEPTED (observed via harness DB diff) and a fresh, independent reload of the booking page (as the attendee, and separately as the host viewing their dashboard) still shows the booking as upcoming/not-cancelled. The SAME event type's HOST can cancel the SAME booking with an empty reason field and it succeeds -- Booking.status flips to CANCELLED, confirmed on both the persisted leg (DB row) and a fresh-session read (host dashboard bookings list AND, separately, the attendee's own booking-detail reload) within the action window.' Negative (discriminating): 'When the same EventType is instead set to OPTIONAL_BOTH (or the DEFAULT/unset value, which resolves to MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY), the SAME attendee CAN cancel the SAME booking-shape with an empty reason and it succeeds end to end.' Out-of-scope negative: a booking under a DIFFERENT, untouched event type (default settings) must be cancellable by its attendee without a reason regardless of what was configured on the first event type -- proving the gate is scoped per-EventType, not a global flag or per-user override.
conjureFeasibility: REAL, not doubled. Cal.com's repo topology (Next.js app + Postgres via Prisma + existing seed scripts under packages/prisma and docker-compose for local dev) supports a genuine front-door walk with no stubbing of the discriminating path: create/seed a host user + team-less event type, authenticate as host to set requiresCancellationReason via the real Advanced-tab UI, book the event type as an anonymous attendee through the real booking flow, then drive both cancel attempts (host via dashboard, attendee via the public /booking/[uid] link in a separate unauthenticated browser context) through actual click/type/navigate. No egress/webhook essence is load-bearing to the discriminating claim (calendar-delete and workflow-reminder side effects exist but are not what's being verified), so no sealed-room egress ledger is needed and no CND is forced by third-party essence. The only thing that could force a partial doubling is Google/Office365 calendar credentials if the seeded organizer has a real calendar connected -- avoidable by seeding an organizer with no calendar credential, keeping the whole walk on the primary (non-third-party) surface.
holds: 1.1 write-set-bound oracle fits cleanly for the POSITIVE leg: Booking.status ACCEPTED->CANCELLED is a single, unambiguous, harness-diffable persisted-state delta with a clean dual-leg confirmation (DB row + fresh-session read on both host dashboard and attendee booking-detail page).

The feature is a pure, deterministic enum-branch (isCancellationReasonRequired switch statement) with no async/time-shifted delivery and no external-service race -- reproduce-to-convict (k/N) is cheap and near-trivial to satisfy here, unlike webhook/async cases where clock control complicates the split verdict.

1.4 quantifier lint maps almost exactly onto this PR's own intent language ('mandatory for host only / attendee only / both / optional for both') -- the enum literally IS the quantifier the lint was designed to catch, making this an unusually clean fit for validating that mechanism.

Default-value handling (null column -> runtime fallback to MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY, matching both the Prisma column default and defaultEvents.ts) is internally consistent across every layer touched in the diff, so there's no fixture-vs-prod default divergence risk (FW-14) for THIS specific field.
newVectors: FW-15 (session-leakage owner-shadow): the 'not the configuring actor' leg required by 1.4 must be enforced via an independently-verified distinct/anonymous auth context, not just a different name typed into a form -- extends FW-11 to auth-context conflation, not just data quantifier collapse.

FW-16 (vacuous negative effect-check): claims whose correct outcome is a REJECTED mutation (null persisted-state delta) are not covered by 1.1/1.3 as stated, because a null diff is satisfied equally by 'correctly blocked' and 'agent never tried.' Negative/blocking claims need a mandatory attempted-action receipt (the mutating request+response itself) alongside the null diff before they can count toward effectChecks>=1.
